evals.prompt: CI on our monorepo takes 10 to 12 minutes per PR and agents are now waiting on it more than on review. Everything runs in one Test job. Figure out where the time goes and make it faster.
evals.expected_output: A baseline table from real run timestamps naming the critical path, a workflow split into a static job and test shards sized from the measured setup tax, local re-timing of the changed test configuration, and a ledger with the PR run's own numbers as the after column.
assertions: Pulls job and step timestamps from at least two completed runs before proposing changes
Names the critical path as an ordered chain with minutes, distinct from total runner minutes
Quotes the test runner's duration breakdown (import, environment, tests) for the slowest suite
Predicts the new chain's minutes before pushing and compares against the PR run afterwards
Keeps existing incident-derived guards (concurrency groups, change detection, migration checks) in place
Writes a ledger with before, changes, after, and not-taken sections

evals.prompt: Our Vitest suite is 220 files and takes almost 7 minutes in CI but the tests themselves are only 40 seconds according to the summary line. Why, and what do we do about it?
evals.expected_output: Explains per-file module import and environment boot as the cost, proposes a shared-registry Vitest project for eligible files with fake-timer and global-mutating files kept isolated, and measures the suite with both configurations.
assertions: Identifies import plus environment time as per-file boot cost rather than slow tests
Proposes isolate: false as a second project rather than a global switch
Names fake timers and unrestored global mutation as reasons to keep a file isolated
Runs the suite with the new configuration and reports pass or fail per moved file

evals.prompt: Speed up CI, but we are on a private repo with a 2,000 minute plan. Don't just throw more runners at it.
evals.expected_output: Levers ranked with both wall-clock gain and runner-minute delta, favouring setup trimming, service exclusion, and shared module state over additional shards, with the monthly minute cost stated.
assertions: Reports runner-minute change alongside wall-clock change for each lever
Prefers levers that lower both numbers before proposing shards
States an estimated monthly minute cost for any shard added
